drills.hint: kataba — past tense, he-form is the dictionary citation form (root k-t-b)
aktubu — present 'I' takes the prefix أ (a-)
tadhhabu — the ta- prefix marks both 'she' and 'you (m.)'
darasnā — past 'we' adds the suffix ـنا (-nā)
yaʾkulūna — masculine plural present ends in ـونَ (-ūna)
uktub — imperative drops the present prefix and adds a helping hamza
māʾ — ends in a hamza on the line
kitāb — from the root k-t-b (writing)
bayt — plural is the broken form buyūt (بُيوت)
kabīr — feminine adds ة: kabīra (كَبيرة)
shukran — reply is ʿafwan (عَفْواً)
al-kitāb — add the article ال; k is a moon letter so the l is pronounced
kabīra — most feminine adjectives add ة (tāʾ marbūṭa)
sayyārat al-mudīr — first noun drops ال, only the last noun keeps it

drills.q: Negate the past 'I went' ('I did not go') in Arabic.
drills.hint: lam adhhab — لم + jussive is the standard past negation
thalātha — the digit is ٣
ʿashara — the digit is ١٠

drills.q: Say 'peace be upon you' (hello) in Arabic.
drills.hint: as-salāmu ʿalaykum — reply wa-ʿalaykum as-salām

drills.q: Ask 'What is your name?' (to a man) in Arabic.
drills.hint: mā-smuk — for a woman say mā-smuki
lā afham — lā negates the present tense
